original_question: Let G be a torsion-free group of type F∞ of infinite cohomological dimension. Must G contain a copy of Thompson’s group F?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.140 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": "Let G be a torsion-free group of type F∞ of infinite cohomological dimension. Must G contain a copy of Thompson’s group F?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it has the same ambient object (a group G), the same three hypotheses (torsion-free, of type F∞, and of infinite cohomological dimension), and the same conclusion asking whether G must contain Thompson’s group F.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, the phrase "type F∞" should be unpacked using the nearby definition in Problem 21.146: G is of type Fn if it has a classifying space with finite n-skeleton, and of type F∞ if this holds for every n.
The idiom "contain a copy of Thompson’s group F" can be made fully explicit as "contain a subgroup isomorphic to Thompson’s group F".

If one wants a notation-level formulation, "of infinite cohomological dimension" may be written as cd(G)=∞; the paper states this condition verbally and does not add further coefficient conventions here.
refined_question: Let G be a torsion-free group of type F∞, meaning that G admits a classifying space K(G,1) whose n-skeleton is finite for every n ≥ 1, and suppose that G has infinite cohomological dimension. Must G contain a subgroup isomorphic to Thompson’s group F?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 21.140 exactly: the wording in the paper is essentially identical. The only nearby contextual material needed for a self-contained restatement is the definition of type Fn and type F∞ given in Problem 21.146 on the same page. The paper does not attach any extra hypotheses, specialized setting, or explicit equivalent reformulation to Problem 21.140, so the faithful refinement is to keep the question exactly this narrow and only spell out the finiteness condition and the phrase "contain a copy."
